criteria.no: The statement adds a new decision the quote leaves open, or asks for something different from the quote.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told whether an extra detail is the obvious reading or a new decision.
criteria.yes: The statement asks for what the quote asks for; any extra detail is only the obvious precise reading of the quote.

faithful.instructions: First identify what `anchor.quote` asks for. Then decide whether `anchor.statement` asks for that same thing, possibly worded more precisely, or adds a new decision. Making the quote precise in the obvious way is not a new decision: the stream a CLI prints to is stdout; logs and error messages go to stdout or stderr; JSON output is a JSON object; a CLI's commands are its subcommands; must replaces should or needs to; concrete values may illustrate a described test; and one directive may be taken from several. A new decision is a choice the quote leaves open, such as a specific algorithm or key strength where the quote only says encrypt, a count, a tool, or a trigger. Naming the same records the quote names, such as paths, commit hashes, codes, or ids, is faithful however many there are. Do not judge vagueness, bundling, or scope.

criteria.no: A required outcome rests on a subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, or an expected output, approval, or standard with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: An outcome is partly concrete, but what to inspect cannot be determined even though nothing is undefined or unrecorded.
criteria.yes: Every required outcome is a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, tool use, or identified record that can be inspected.

observable.instructions: Can each outcome that `anchor.statement` requires be checked by inspecting something concrete: a behavior, output, exit status, file, path, value, tool used, or an identified record? Bundled duties, added details, and informal wording do not matter here. Nothing can be inspected for a subjective quality (robust), a label, tier, or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K, 'the gold-tier store'), including one that names where results must go, an expected output, approval, or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's say-so with no identified record. A mode the statement defines inline is inspectable.

criteria.no: No subject is named; the requirement applies to nothing identifiable.
criteria.unclear: A subject is hinted at but cannot be identified.
criteria.yes: A subject (component, artifact, process, path, or explicit set) is named.

scoped.instructions: Does `anchor.statement` or `anchor.scope` name the subject the requirement applies to, such as a command, module, service, pipeline, artifact, process, path, or an explicit 'all' or 'every' set? A named subject is enough even when the requirement about it is vague or poorly worded.

criteria.no: A decisive term is a subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, an unidentified expected output or standard, or an approval with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it is decisive.
criteria.yes: Every decisive term can be understood from the statement or common technical knowledge.

self_contained.instructions: Can each decisive term in `anchor.statement` be understood from the statement itself or from common technical knowledge? Understood terms include commands, subcommands, flags, files, paths, values, environment variables, formats, streams, roles such as 'the caller', and terms the statement defines inline. Bundled duties, added details, sentence form, and who is told to act (a named component, 'you', or nobody) do not matter here. A term cannot be understood when it is a subjective quality (robust), a label or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's approval with no identified record. Judge each decisive term separately: one undefined label, tier, or mode, or one subjective quality, makes the answer no even when the statement also names many concrete paths, hashes, codes, or ids.

criteria.no: The statement joins two or more required actions, or two subjects each with its own action, so one part could be met while another is not.
criteria.unclear: The parts could equally be read as one action with several targets or as separate actions.
criteria.yes: One subject has one required action or one prohibition; any list only enumerates the targets, surfaces, values, or conditions of that same action.

single_constraint.instructions: Does `anchor.statement` impose one requirement rather than several separate ones? It is one requirement when every listed target, output stream, file, value, or condition qualifies the same required action or prohibition of the same subject; for example, 'must omit X from stdout, stderr and saved files' is one requirement. It is several requirements when it joins separate required actions that could each be met while the other is not; for example, 'the CLI must emit JSON and the daemon must write an audit log'. Judge only this; ignore vagueness, fidelity to the quote, and scope.

criteria.no: Adds a choice the quote leaves open, or requires something different.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told whether an added detail is obvious precision or a new choice.
criteria.yes: Same requirement as the quote, with at most obvious precision.

faithful.instructions: Compare `anchor.statement` with `anchor.quote`. Answer whether the statement requires the same thing the quote requires, allowing obvious precision: must for should or needs to, stdout as a CLI's print stream, subcommands as a CLI's commands, a JSON object for JSON output, illustrative concrete values, taking one directive out of several, and repeating the records the quote names (paths, hashes, codes, ids). It is unfaithful only when the statement settles something the quote leaves open (an algorithm, key strength, count, tool, or trigger) or requires something different. Ignore vagueness, bundling, and scope.

criteria.no: Some required outcome depends on a subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, or an unidentified baseline, expected output, approval, or standard.
criteria.unclear: Some outcome is partly concrete but what to inspect cannot be determined, though nothing is undefined or unidentified.
criteria.yes: Every required outcome can be checked against something concrete or an identified record.

observable.instructions: Could a reviewer check compliance with `anchor.statement` by inspecting something concrete: a behavior, output, exit status, file, path, value, tool used, or an identified record such as a named release, tag, report id, or commit? Ignore bundling, added details, and wording style. Compliance cannot be inspected when it depends on a subjective quality (robust, clean), a label, tier, or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), or a baseline, expected output, approval, or standard that the statement does not identify by a record ('like before', 'the expected output', 'the approved ones'). A mode or exception list given inline is inspectable.

criteria.no: Nothing identifiable is named as the subject.
criteria.unclear: A subject is hinted at but cannot be identified.

scoped.instructions: Is there a named subject the requirement applies to, in `anchor.statement` or `anchor.scope`: a command, module, service, pipeline, artifact, process, path, mode, or an explicit 'all'/'every' set? Naming the subject is enough; do not judge how well the requirement is written.

criteria.no: Some decisive term is subjective, undefined, unidentified, or an unrecorded approval.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it is decisive.
criteria.yes: Every decisive term is understood from the statement or common technical knowledge.

self_contained.instructions: Check every decisive term of `anchor.statement` one by one. A term is understood if it is common technical knowledge (commands, subcommands, flags, files, paths, values, environment variables, formats, streams, roles like 'the caller'), a named record (release tag, report id, commit), or defined inline in the statement. A term is not understood if it is a subjective quality (robust), an undefined label or mode (R7, Mode K), a baseline, expected output, or standard not identified by a record ('before', 'the expected output'), or an approval with no identified record. One such term makes the answer no, however many concrete terms surround it. Ignore bundling, added details, sentence form, and who is told to act.

criteria.no: Two or more duties that could each be met while another is not.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be decided whether the parts are one duty with several targets or separate duties.
criteria.yes: Exactly one duty; any list only enumerates targets or conditions of that duty.

single_constraint.instructions: Count the separate duties in `anchor.statement`. A duty is one required action or one prohibition of one subject. A list of targets, streams, files, values, or conditions for that same action is still one duty ('must omit X from stdout, stderr and saved files'). Two actions, or two subjects each with an action, that could be satisfied independently are two duties ('the CLI must emit JSON and the daemon must write an audit log'). Do not judge vagueness, the quote, or scope.

criteria.no: A new decision or a different demand.
criteria.unclear: Cannot tell whether a detail is obvious precision or a new decision.
criteria.yes: Same demand as the quote, at most obviously more precise.

faithful.instructions: Does `anchor.statement` ask for the same thing as `anchor.quote`? Obvious precise readings are the same thing (must for should; stdout for where a CLI prints; subcommands for a CLI's commands; one directive selected from several; the same named records; illustrative values for a described test). A new decision the quote leaves open (algorithm, strength, count, tool, trigger) or a different demand is not. Do not judge vagueness, bundling, or scope.

criteria.no: At least one required outcome rests on something subjective, undefined, or unidentified.
criteria.unclear: An outcome is partly concrete but what to inspect cannot be determined, with nothing undefined or unidentified.
criteria.yes: Each required outcome has something concrete or an identified record to inspect.

observable.instructions: Step 1: list each outcome `anchor.statement` requires. Step 2: for each, name what a reviewer would inspect (behavior, output, exit status, file, path, value, tool use, or an identified record). Step 3: if any outcome has nothing nameable to inspect because it rests on a subjective quality, an undefined label/tier/mode, or an unidentified baseline, expected output, approval, or standard, answer no. Inline definitions and inline exception lists count as inspectable. Ignore bundling and style.

criteria.unclear: A subject is hinted at but cannot be identified.

scoped.instructions: Name the subject that `anchor.statement` or `anchor.scope` constrains (command, module, service, pipeline, artifact, process, path, or explicit all/every set). If one is named, the answer is yes regardless of requirement quality.

criteria.no: A decisive term is subjective, undefined, unidentified, or an unrecorded approval.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it is decisive.
criteria.yes: Every decisive term is understood without outside context.

self_contained.instructions: Could an engineer with common technical knowledge and no other context understand every decisive term of `anchor.statement`? Commands, flags, files, paths, values, formats, streams, roles, named releases/tags/report ids, and inline-defined terms are understood. A subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, an unidentified baseline/expected output/standard, or an approval with no identified record is not, and one such decisive term makes the answer no. Ignore bundling, added details, form, and who acts.

criteria.no: Separate actions or subjects that could pass and fail independently.
criteria.unclear: Equally readable as one action with several targets or as separate actions.
criteria.yes: Single action or prohibition of one subject; lists only qualify it.

single_constraint.instructions: Imagine checking `anchor.statement`. Could one part pass while another fails because they are different actions or belong to different subjects? If every listed item only names a target, stream, file, value, or condition of one action or prohibition, it is a single constraint. Judge only that.
